From the text, each row and column must contain exactly two R and two G. Since row 1 already has two R, fill r1c2 and r1c4 with G. Since column 3 already has two R at rows 1 and 2, fill r3c3 and r4c3 with G. Row 3 then has G at c3 and c4, so r3c1 and r3c2 must be R. Column 4 has G at rows 1 and 3, so r2c4 and r4c4 must be R. Row 2 then has R at c3 and c4, so r2c1 and r2c2 must be G. Finally, column 1 has R,G,R in rows 1–3, so r4c1=G; column 2 has G,G,R in rows 1–3, so r4c2=R. Therefore the lowest row is GRGR.

Column 3 then has R in rows 1 and 2, so rows 3 and 4 in column 3 must be G. Row 3 now has G in columns 3 and 4, so its only valid row pattern is RRGG. Column 4 now has G in rows 1 and 3, so rows 2 and 4 in column 4 must be R. Row 2, with R in columns 3 and 4, is forced to GGRR. Now compute the bottom row as the missing colour in each column after the top three rows are known: column 1 has R,G,R so bottom is G; column 2 has G,G,R so bottom is R; column 3 has R,R,G so bottom is G; column 4 has G,R,G so bottom is R. Thus the lowest row is GRGR.
